column1: # thruline musl artefacts — CONSUMED from Track C, COPIED into this lane.
# WHY THE COPY EXISTS (DECISIONS #62). These were read live from
# /Users/dev/thruline-gate/target/musl, inside another track's
# gitignored build directory. Track C reaped that directory and stopped one
# path short of deleting them; `cargo clean` — the obvious reading of "reap
# your build directory" — would have taken them mid-pilot. An artefact one
# track consumes must not live where another track's housekeeping reaches.
# I ARGUED THE OTHER WAY AND I WAS WRONG. I told Track C to leave them in
# place because "a copy would be a second artefact with no provenance". The
# answer is to carry the provenance WITH the copy, which is this file — not
# to avoid copying and hope nobody sweeps.
# The binaries live in fixtures/bench/musl/, which .gitignore:10 excludes
# (43 MB); this manifest is committed beside them, exactly as
# fixtures/bench/download.sh pins the Terminal-Bench tarball by sha256.
# scripts/pilot-run.sh verifies every staged binary against these digests
# and REFUSES on a mismatch: an unpinned artefact in a lane is the same
# liability one directory along.
# producer: Track C, worktree ~/thruline-gate, branch codex/m6-gate-packaging
# built by: ./packaging/build-musl.sh, rust:1.97.1-alpine, --locked,
#           --no-default-features (ORT has no musl build)
# Verified independently in this lane, by property and not by phrasing:
#   readelf -l -> 0 INTERP segments; readelf -d -> 0 NEEDED entries
#   aarch64 runs `--version` in ghcr.io/laude-institute/t-bench/python-3-13:20250620
#   NOTE: `file` says "statically linked" for aarch64 and "static-pie
#   linked" for x86_64. Both are static. A check on that string refuses the
#   amd64 artefact, and `ldd` on the static-pie prints a loader path that is
#   not a dependency — which fails in the UNSAFE direction.
# arch
aarch64
